text: dsh-windows-mcp 是面向 DeepSeek Harness Desktop 的 Windows 桌面自动化插件，通过 Cordis patch 挂载 DSH 内置 MCP 客户端并连接 Windows-MCP。它提供桌面工具桥接、可持久化的 Computer Use 开关、按会话延迟揭示工具、依赖安装与镜像选择、版本检查及回滚，并带有诊断工具和设置页面。适合希望让 DSH agent 查看屏幕、操作鼠标键盘、使用剪贴板或管理进程的 Windows 用户。安装 Windows-MCP 需要本机 uv；桌面控制默认关闭。

dsh-windows-mcp connects Windows-MCP to DeepSeek Harness through its in-box MCP bridge. It adds a Computer Use switch, lazy tool reveal, installation, updates, rollback, and diagnostics. Windows users can let DSH inspect screens and use input, clipboard, and process tools. uv is required.
想让 DSH agent 看见 Windows 桌面并根据截图回答。
我想让 DSH 控制鼠标、键盘并操作桌面界面。
有没有办法从 DSH 读取窗口的无障碍树和文本？
让 DSH 可以读写 Windows 剪贴板。
我需要让 DSH agent 查看和管理本机进程。
希望按需展示桌面工具，避免每轮都带很多工具定义。
想从 DSH 设置页安装或更新 Windows-MCP，并能回滚版本。
How can my DSH agent inspect and interact with a Windows desktop?
I want to expose Windows screenshots, clicks, typing, and clipboard through MCP.
Can I install and roll back the Windows-MCP dependency from a DSH settings page?
dsh-windows-mcp 的功能「Computer Use 开关」：composer 中的 Computer Use pill 读取并更新宿主持久化状态；关闭时过滤桥接工具并阻止调用。
dsh-windows-mcp 的功能「按需展示桌面工具」：默认先提供 windows_desktop 单一入口，可按请求揭示桥接工具，并在后续步骤提供工具定义。
dsh-windows-mcp 的功能「桌面桥接诊断」：windows_mcp_doctor 报告依赖、有效桥接配置和当前注册的 Windows 工具，帮助定位工具缺失。
dsh-windows-mcp 的功能「安装 Windows-MCP」：设置界面可检查依赖并启动 uv 安装；依赖状态和安装进度由宿主路由提供。
dsh-windows-mcp 的功能「镜像检查与版本更新」：更新管理器探测 PyPI 镜像、读取可用版本，并可安装、激活或回滚已安装版本。
dsh-windows-mcp 的功能「配置桥接和插件选项」：设置页调整超时、截图缩放、捕获后端、排除工具、镜像策略和延迟工具开关；桥接配置写入 profile patch。

**Windows desktop automation for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/sandbaseai/deepseek-harness-handbook)** — lets the DSH agent see your screen and drive your PC.

dsh-windows-mcp README · dsh-windows-mcp：This plugin connects [CursorTouch/Windows-MCP](https://github.com/CursorTouch/Windows-MCP) to DSH by mounting one loader row against the **MCP client bridge that already ships inside DeepSeek Harness**. There is no reimplemented protocol client and no second copy of the MCP SDK: the plugin is a *carrier bundle*, and everything you can do comes from the official bridge.

dsh-windows-mcp README · dsh-windows-mcp：```text
DSH agent
  └─ tool call  mcp__windows__Screenshot
       └─ @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client        (in-box, mounted by this plugin's patch row)
            └─ uvx windows-mcp@0.8.8 serve   (stdio child process)

dsh-windows-mcp README · What it gives the agent：Plus one tool of its own, `windows_mcp_doctor`, which explains what is wrong when the `mcp__windows__*` tools are missing.

The composer also gains a **Computer Use** pill, next to the permission control: it shows how many desktop tools are actually registered and remembers your choice across restarts (state file: `~/.dsh/dsh-windows-mcp.state.json`). It starts **off** — a fresh install never hands the agent your desktop until you switch the pill on yourself.

dsh-windows-mcp README · What it gives the agent：Switching it off is a hard switch, not a hint. The bridge keeps running, but from the next step on every `mcp__windows__*` tool is filtered out of the tool list the model sees, and a call that still names one is refused at dispatch — in every session and subagent, live, with no restart. Switch it back on and they return immediately; `windows_mcp_doctor` always reports which way it is set.

dsh-windows-mcp README · What it gives the agent：> **Verified:** Windows 11 + DSH Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2 — the bridged server advertises
> **18 tools** (the 21 upstream tools minus the three excluded here) and is ready
> about 1.5 s after launch. The bridge publishes each as `mcp__windows__<ToolName>`.

dsh-windows-mcp README · Requirements：- **Windows 10/11.**
- **DeepSeek Harness Desktop** with the in-box `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` bridge (0.2.0-rc.2 or newer).
- **[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)** on the `PATH` of the process that runs DSH — **Settings → Desktop** uses it to install Windows-MCP. DSH itself boots without it. `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` is searched even when it is not on `PATH`.
- **A model that accepts image input** if you want the agent to actually *see* screenshots.

dsh-windows-mcp README · Boot is never blocked by the dependency：The bridge row ships **disabled**, on purpose. A `uvx`-style first launch
resolves Windows-MCP's Python dependencies from the package index, and on a slow
or blocked network that resolve can sit inside DSH's startup for minutes — the
window stays on “Loading plugins…”. A plugin must never be able to do that to
its host, so:
section: Boot is never blocked by the dependency

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · Boot is never blocked by the dependency：- **First boot after installing the bundle:** DSH starts normally, no Windows
  tools yet, and the dependency is reported as *not installed* — both on the
  Plugins page and in **Settings → Desktop**.
- **Install it from Settings → Desktop** (next section). It probes PyPI mirrors,
  installs into the plugin's own toolchain directory, and rewrites the bridge row
  with `disabled: false` and `command:` pointing at the installed executable.
- **Restart DSH once.** From then on the bridge spawns the exe directly — on
  Windows 11 the server is ready about **1.5 s** after launch, with no network.
section: Boot is never blocked by the dependency

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · Boot is never blocked by the dependency：`uv` is only needed by the installer. On a restricted network, point `uv` at a
mirror once (`%APPDATA%\uv\uv.toml`) and the manual/CLI paths get the same
speed-up:

```toml
default-index = "https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple"
```
section: Boot is never blocked by the dependency

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · Install：The plugin is a normal DSH bundle. Install it with DSH's own plugin manager:

1. Open **DSH Desktop → Settings → Plugins**.
2. Add the bundle, pointing at either the published package name, the repository (`github:helloHub1212/dsh-windows-mcp`), or a local checkout of this repo.
3. **Restart DSH** so the new patch layer is composed at startup.

For non-Electron profiles the CLI does the same thing:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:helloHub1212/dsh-windows-mcp
```
dsh-windows-mcp README · Install：> The Electron app owns the `desktop` profile; the CLI refuses every command against it, including read-only ones. Use the GUI for `desktop`.
dsh-windows-mcp README · Install the dependency from the app：Windows-MCP itself is a Python program, so the **Dependency** card in **Settings → Desktop** shows its state and installs it for you:
section: Install the dependency from the app

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · Install the dependency from the app：- **Dependency** — `installed 0.8.8`, or *not installed*, or *uv not found*.
- **Download and install** — runs `uv tool install windows-mcp@<pinned>` once (through the fastest mirror), streams the installer output into the page, and offers **Cancel** while it runs.
- When it finishes, the plugin **writes the bridge row into your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` itself** — after a timestamped backup, inside idempotent markers — with `disabled: false` and `command:` pointing at the installed executable. **Restart DSH** to apply that; from then on the bridge launches the exe directly and never resolves a package index during boot.
section: Install the dependency from the app

text: dsh-windows-mcp README · Install the dependency from the app：The block it writes is the row documented under [Pin a local interpreter instead of `uvx`](#pin-a-local-interpreter-instead-of-uvx); delete the marked block to return to the inert, `uvx`-based row. The plugin's own page in **Settings → Plugins** keeps a one-line status that points here, and the activation prompt shown after enabling the bundle offers the same install button.
section: Install the dependency from the app

text: dsh-windows-mcp README · Install the dependency from the app：The page also shows the **Patch target**: the `cordis.patch.yml` a manual write would touch, which is the profile this host booted — including a `dsh --profile web` host. If this package sits in more than one profile and the host does not report which one it started, the plugin writes nothing and says so instead of guessing: set `DSH_WINDOWS_MCP_PROFILE=<profile name>` (or an absolute profile directory) for the process that runs DSH and retry.
section: Install the dependency from the app

text: dsh-windows-mcp README · Update Windows-MCP, and roll back：The same page manages the upstream version, so an upgrade never means reinstalling the dependency by hand:

dsh-windows-mcp README · Update Windows-MCP, and roll back：- **It checks by itself.** On boot, and whenever the page asks, the plugin probes the PyPI mirrors, takes the fastest one that answers and reads its `windows-mcp` index. The result is cached for six hours in `$DSH_HOME/dsh-windows-mcp.versions.json`, so restarts do not hammer the network.
- **Versions live side by side.** Every version is installed into its own tool root, `$DSH_HOME/dsh-windows-mcp/toolchain/<version>/windows-mcp`, through `UV_TOOL_DIR`. Activating a version only rewrites the bridge row (backed up, as above): no reinstall, and the previous version stays on disk.
- **Update in one click.** **Update to vX** downloads that version from the fastest mirror that works, verifies the executable and its `dist-info`, then activates it — the panel names the running version and the mirror it came from.
- **Roll back the same way.** **Roll back to vPrev** points the bridge back at the version the active one replaced; nothing is downloaded.

dsh-windows-mcp README · Update Windows-MCP, and roll back：Only managed installs are used by the bridge: it stays disabled until an install (or **Point the bridge at it**) rewrites the row with a real executable, and the panel says which side is live (`uv-tool` vs `managed`).

dsh-windows-mcp README · Fast mirrors for the Python dependency：The check measures all seven candidates — PyPI plus the USTC, Aliyun, Tencent Cloud, Huawei Cloud, Nanjing University and TUNA mirrors — with a 96 KiB ranged read, and ranks them by throughput. An install uses the fastest mirror that works and falls back to the next one when a mirror fails, with `UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS=4`, `UV_HTTP_RETRIES=3` and `UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT=600`, because mirrors rate-limit uv's default of eight parallel downloads (HTTP 429). A mirror that has blocked this network is ranked out instead of failing the install; the measured speed is shown per mirror in the panel.
section: Fast mirrors for the Python dependency

text: dsh-windows-mcp README · Settings page and the star button：Everything above, plus a few knobs that do not belong on a plugin card, lives in **Settings → Desktop** — a new entry in the settings sidebar, next to the other plugins' pages:
section: Settings page and the star button

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · Settings page and the star button：- **Dependency** — install, reinstall, update, roll back, and a **Point the bridge at it** action, with the live installer log and the patched row's target. The plugin's own page only carries a pointer to this card.
- **Bridge** — `toolCallTimeoutMs`, the screenshot scale, the capture backend, upstream's flash overlay, and the three tools the bridge may exclude (`App`, `PowerShell`, `FileSystem`). These are written into the bridge row of your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (timestamped backup first), so **they apply after DSH restarts**; the page states which row is in effect.
- **Updates** — whether the plugin checks for a newer Windows-MCP on boot, and the mirror policy: `auto` keeps the measured ranking, an explicit mirror pins it, and the official index always stays as the last resort.
- **Tool exposure** — **Lazy tools** (on by default): the model sees a single `windows_desktop` entry instead of eighteen schemas, calls it, and from the next step the desktop tools it revealed are in the tool table. Turn it off to send every schema on every step.
- **About** — the plugin version, the repository link, and a **Star** button
section: Settings page and the star button

text: dsh-windows-mcp README · Settings page and the star button：Saving is atomic (`$DSH_HOME/dsh-windows-mcp.settings.json`). A value out of range is clamped to its default and reported instead of being written silently, and a change that leaves the bridge row untouched does not rewrite the patch layer at all. **Revert** restores the defaults in the form.
section: Settings page and the star button

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · Lazy tools：Eighteen tool schemas cost context on every step, including the steps where nobody touches the desktop. With lazy tools on (the default), the model is offered one entry:

> `windows_desktop` — *Reveal the Windows desktop capabilities (screenshots, clicking, typing, windows, clipboard, processes) for this session.*

dsh-windows-mcp README · Lazy tools：Calling it with no arguments reveals every capability for that session; `{"query": "screenshot"}` or `{"names": ["mcp__windows__Click"]}` narrows it. The definitions come back in the tool result and the revealed tools join the tool table on the next step, so the choice survives until the session ends. A hidden tool that gets called anyway is refused with a hint to reveal first.

dsh-windows-mcp README · Lazy tools：Revelation is per session, and the switch is honest both ways: with **Computer Use** off the entry is hidden too, and nothing can be revealed behind the human's back.

dsh-windows-mcp README · The welcome dialog：The first time the bundle is enabled — and on every later enable from the Plugins page — a **Welcome to the DSH desktop automation plugin** dialog is raised over the whole window: a frosted sheet on a blurred scrim that leaves the app's own DOM and mounts on `document.body`, so nothing in the page can clip or bury it. It says, in three lines, where the dependency (install, update, rollback) and the parameters live (**Settings → Desktop**), and where the **Computer Use** switch is, and it carries a prominent **Star on GitHub** button. Escape, the backdrop or *Got it* dismisses it; focus is trapped inside while it is open, and a CLI/config enable shows it once per browser instead of every time.

dsh-windows-mcp README · Verify：```text
windows_mcp_doctor
```

Prints the resolved `uv`/`uvx`/`python`, the state of `%USERPROFILE%\.windows-mcp`, the effective bridge row, and the `mcp__windows__*` tools that are actually registered. Then ask the agent:

> Take a screenshot of my desktop and tell me what is on screen.
dsh-windows-mcp README · Configuration：The defaults live in [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml). Everything below is set through the `env` block of the `windows-mcp-bridge` row.

dsh-windows-mcp README · Configuration：| Variable | Default here | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WINDOWS_MCP_SCREENSHOT_SCALE` | `0.75` | Screenshot downscale, `0.1`–`1.0`. The single biggest lever on image token cost. |
| `WINDOWS_MCP_DISABLE_FLASH` | `1` | Suppresses upstream's orange "control taken over" border on every capture. |
| `WINDOWS_MCP_SCREENSHOT_BACKEND` | `auto` | Capture backend; see upstream docs before overriding. |
| `WINDOWS_MCP_MAX_TREE_ELEMENTS` | `500` | Cap on the accessibility-tree size reported by `Snapshot`. |
| `WINDOWS_MCP_WATCHDOG` | `off` | Upstream watchdog. Off by default because the UIA event pump can take the whole process down ([upstream #332](https://github.com/CursorTouch/Windows-MCP/issues/332)). |
| `ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY` | `false` | Upstream defaults to **on** (PostHog). This plugin turns it off. |

dsh-windows-mcp README · Override the row from your profile：Do not edit the plugin's own file — patch the row by id from your profile's
`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, which is composed *after* bundle
rows and therefore wins.
section: Override the row from your profile

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · Override the row from your profile：**A patch replaces the whole `config` object; it does not deep-merge it.** The
loader applies overrides as `target[key] = value` (`applyEntryPatches` in
`dsh-app-boot`), so a key you leave out is a key you delete: `serverName` is
required (and names every tool), `transport` is required, `command` is required
for `stdio`, `url` for `streamable-http`. A patch whose `id` does not exist, or
whose `name` does not match, is skipped with a warning instead of failing.

```yaml
section: Override the row from your profile

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · $DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml — the complete row：- id: windows-mcp-bridge
  config:
    serverName: windows
    transport: stdio
    command: uvx
    args: [windows-mcp@0.8.8, serve, --exclude-tools, "App,PowerShell,FileSystem"]
    toolCallTimeoutMs: 120000
    failOnStartupError: false
    reconnect: { enabled: true, initialDelayMs: 500, maxDelayMs: 30000, maxAttempts: 10 }
    env:
      ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY: "false"
      WINDOWS_MCP_DISABLE_FLASH: "1"
      WINDOWS_MCP_SCREENSHOT_SCALE: "0.5"
```

dsh-windows-mcp README · $DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml — the complete row：`--exclude-tools` takes its names as one comma-separated argument
(`"App,PowerShell,FileSystem"`), and `ControlStatus` is always kept — upstream
offers no way to exclude it.

dsh-windows-mcp README · Pin a local interpreter instead of `uvx`：`uvx` re-resolves the package on every launch. For a reproducible setup, install
it once (`uv tool install windows-mcp`) or use any Python that already has it,
and change `command`/`args` in the complete row above:

```yaml
- id: windows-mcp-bridge
  config:
    serverName: windows
    transport: stdio
section: Pin a local interpreter instead of `uvx`

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · Use a long-lived HTTP server instead：Windows-MCP can also run as a background server. Upstream's `windows-mcp install`
registers an ONLOGON scheduled task that serves **streamable-http** on
`127.0.0.1:8000`; switch the row to match — this variant has `url` instead of
`command`/`args`/`env`:

```yaml
- id: windows-mcp-bridge
  config:
    serverName: windows
    transport: streamable-http
section: Use a long-lived HTTP server instead

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · Use a long-lived HTTP server instead：There is no `env` field in this variant, so the telemetry and flash defaults no
longer apply to the server: start it yourself with `ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false`
and `WINDOWS_MCP_DISABLE_FLASH=1` if you want the same behaviour.
section: Use a long-lived HTTP server instead

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · Use a long-lived HTTP server instead：This survives DSH restarts and skips per-launch startup cost, at the price of a
process that outlives the app. Two upstream caveats: `install` binds the
scheduled task to the interpreter it was run from (installing from a temporary
`uvx` environment registers a task pointing at a cache directory that `uv` may
reclaim — install with `uv tool install windows-mcp` or a fixed venv instead),
and non-loopback hosts refuse to start without `--auth-key`/`--oauth-client-id`
or an explicit `--allow-insecure-remote`.
section: Use a long-lived HTTP server instead

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Likely cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| No `mcp__windows__*` tools at all | Run `windows_mcp_doctor`. On a fresh install that is expected: the bridge ships disabled until you install the dependency from **Settings → Desktop** and restart DSH. If it is installed already, the doctor prints the effective row — look for `disabled` / `command` — and the host log carries `mcp-client(windows)` lines. |
| Tools disappeared after an upgrade | The tool names are `mcp__<serverName>__<tool>`. Changing `serverName` changes every tool name (and breaks the prompt cache prefix). |
| Screenshots come back as text | The active model does not accept image input, or attachments are disabled in your harness configuration. Upstream images are only projected when admission succeeds. |
| `App` tool fails or returns nothing | Upstream documents it as reliable on English Windows installs only; it is excluded by default. |
| DSH takes noticeably longer to boot | The bridge should not cost boot time: it ships `disabled: true` and only starts once an install has pointed it at an executable. A slow boot means some *other* row is resolving a toolchain at boot —

dsh-windows-mcp README · Security：This plugin hands the model your mouse, your keyboard, your clipboard, your
processes and your registry. Treat installing it as handing over control of the
desktop session it runs in.

What the design does and does not do:

dsh-windows-mcp README · Security：- **No network exposure by default.** The default row is stdio: a child process
  connected by pipes, not a listening socket.
- **Secret hygiene on the child process.** The bridge starts MCP children from a
  scrubbed environment: variable names matching `KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN` and
  **all** `DSH_*` variables are removed before the configured `env` is merged in.
  Credentials should therefore be passed explicitly through the row's `env`, not
  inherited.
- **No telemetry from this plugin.** Upstream's own PostHog reporting is
  explicitly disabled in the shipped defaults.
- **Remote serving is upstream's problem, not a hidden default.** If you switch
  to HTTP, upstream enforces loopback host filtering and refuses to start on a
  non-loopback address without an auth key.
- **Switch flips are a window decision, not a network one.** Every mutating
  route (`/state`, `/prepare`, `/prepare/cancel`, `/bridge`, `/update`,
  `/settings`) requires the signed session cookie the DSH window receives during
  the launch-token exchange; without it the request is refused with `401`. A
  script, `curl`, or a model with shell access cannot turn desktop control

dsh-windows-mcp README · How it works：DeepSeek Harness plugins are loader patches, and a patch row may mount a package
that lives inside the Electron `app.asar` — the loader resolves official
`@deepseek-ai/*` names from the Desktop install anchor. Third-party code cannot
`import` those packages, but it *can* name them in a patch, because the mount
happens inside the loader rather than inside plugin code. That is the whole trick
behind this package:

dsh-windows-mcp README · How it works：```yaml
- insert:
    - id: windows-mcp-plugin
      name: dsh-windows-mcp                  # lib/index.js: doctor tool + startup audit
    - id: windows-mcp-bridge

Consequences worth knowing:

dsh-windows-mcp README · How it works：- The integration is **version-sensitive** in one direction only: the bridge
  config schema belongs to DSH, not to this plugin. `package.json` declares the
  patch; DSH decides how to read it.
- Image projection is a bridge feature: MCP image blocks are saved as DSH
  attachments and surfaced as native image content. Audio and embedded resources
  degrade to diagnostic text.
- **MCP prompts are not supported** by the bridge (resources are, on demand).

dsh-windows-mcp README · Development：```powershell
npm install
npm test          # node --test, including a real YAML parse of the patch
npm run check     # node --check lib/index.js
```

To see the composed config without touching a live profile — and without
restarting DSH — use the dump harness:

```powershell

dsh-windows-mcp README · one-time: a scratch profile with the real profile's node_modules：mkdir  $env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\dtest
copy   $env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop\package.json $env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\dtest\
cmd /c mklink /J $env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\dtest\node_modules $env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules

npm run dump
```

section: one-time: a scratch profile with the real profile's node_modules

text:
dsh-windows-mcp README · one-time: a scratch profile with the real profile's node_modules：```text
cordis.patch.yml      the integration: two insert rows
lib/index.js          host half: routes + windows_mcp_doctor + startup audit (no dependencies)
lib/dependency.js     dependency state, uv invocation, profile bridge-row writer
lib/pypi.js           PyPI index parsing and version maths (pure functions)
lib/mirrors.js        mirror candidates, ranged speed probe, ranking
lib/installs.js       per-version tool roots and the versions state file
lib/updater.js        version manager: check / install / activate / roll back
lib/settings.js       user settings: validation, storage, bridge round-trip
lib/client.js         web half: composer switch, plugin panel, settings page
test/plugin.test.mjs  patch composition + hostile-context + panel tests
test/update.test.mjs  version maths, mirror ranking, isolation and rollback state machine
test/settings.test.mjs  settings validation, bridge round-trip, settings route
scripts/dump-config.mjs  dev helper for composing against a scratch profile
